analysis:
Examined all supplied patches, BASE/HEAD source and metadata against the canonical definition index and selected TB-002/TB-011 details. No independently supported security regression in this scope. ProviderLoop+AutopilotBusy.swift:11-33 preserves every predicate in the former admission busy check; excluding the accepted autopilot operation permits its existing pre-mutation revalidation, while concurrent commands remain rejected in ProviderLoop+Autopilot.swift:117-124. New report fields and replayed status detail are consent-gated (:57-80, :277), including private-only exclusion in ProviderLoop+AutopilotControl.swift:8-10. Added cancellation checks (:217, :224) prevent success/lease recording after cooperative cancellation. Command equality, bounded result history, ownership, memory feasibility and hardware checks remain. Control.swift:31 only changes tuple access.
Material integration questions remain: AutopilotInventory.swift HEAD patch lines 10-15 allows valid adoption to retain advertisements without a live control lease. Inspect autopilotAdoptionIsValid, adoption issuance/revocation and autopilotAllowsModel interactions (Control.swift:46-54) to establish that retained advertisement does not widen consented serving or cold-load eligibility. Inspect reconcileAutopilotPlacements and recordAutopilotPlacement (Autopilot.swift:21, :228), and beginModelAdvertisementOccurrence (Inventory.swift HEAD patch :69) with transition-watchdog ownership/retirement and report bounds. Their implementations are outside this evidence, not observed missing controls. Validate stall recovery preserves resource ownership until native work settles and cannot clear another operation's admission fence. Relevant contracts are TB-002/TB-007 availability and model policy, TB-011/T-053 live authorization, and T-056's prohibition on treating provider-origin reports as trusted evidence or reward qualification. No encryption, credential, attestation or billing implementation changes are visible here; downstream consumption of new reports needs integration review.
